items.title: The Catalan Twelve: Twelve Recipes, Recovered
items.author: Donnie Boman
items.description:
No one can prove the Catalan Twelve exist. That has never stopped them from taking credit, or avoiding it, for centuries. The same dough technique, the same insistence on cold butter, keeps turning up in kitchens that have no business knowing each other. Twelve real, fully tested recipes, from Girona xuxos to the Moon Pie, come with recovered ledger fragments and a reading list that isn't lying to you about everything. Underneath the conspiracy is a quieter story: one baker from the Gulf Coast, insisting that the place mattered. Believe the rest if you like.

It is, at once, a cookbook, a fake archival investigation, a comedy about provenance, and a memoir about inheritance, loss, and the fragile ways practical knowledge moves from one person to another. It understands that names drift, traditions are often invented after the fact, and recipes outlive their authors by belonging to whoever makes them next.

items.title: The Cooking Gene
items.subtitle: A Journey Through African American Culinary History in the Old South
items.author: Michael Twitty
items.description:
For the parts of The Catalan Twelve that transcended even the Society, or whomever.

Southern food is integral to the American culinary tradition, yet the question of who "owns" it is one of the most provocative touch points in our ongoing struggles over race. In this unique memoir, culinary historian Michael W. Twitty takes readers to the white-hot center of this fight, tracing the roots of his own family and the charged politics surrounding the origins of soul food, barbecue, and all Southern cuisine.

items.title: BraveTart
items.subtitle: Iconic American Desserts
items.author: Stella Parks
items.description:
A history of American desserts that takes apart their origin stories, usually in favor of something messier and better documented.

From One-Bowl Devil’s Food Layer Cake to a flawless Cherry Pie that’s crisp even on the very bottom, BraveTart is a celebration of classic American desserts. Whether down-home delights like Blueberry Muffins and Glossy Fudge Brownies or supermarket mainstays such as Vanilla Wafers and Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough Ice Cream, your favorites are all here. These meticulously tested recipes bring an award-winning pastry chef’s expertise into your kitchen, along with advice on how to “mix it up” with over 200 customizable variations—in short, exactly what you’d expect from a cookbook penned by a senior editor at Serious Eats. Yet BraveTart is much more than a cookbook, as Stella Parks delves into the surprising stories of how our favorite desserts came to be, from chocolate chip cookies that predate the Tollhouse Inn to the prohibition-era origins of ice cream sodas and floats.

items.title: On Food and Cooking
items.subtitle: The Science and Lore of the Kitchen
items.author: Harold McGee
items.description:
For anyone who wants the actual chemistry behind why cold fat laminates, why gelatin sets, and why browned butter smells the way it does, this is the reference The Catalan Twelve is quietly leaning on.

On Food and Cooking pioneered the translation of technical food science into cook-friendly kitchen science and helped birth the inventive culinary movement known as "molecular gastronomy." Though other books have been written about kitchen science, On Food and Cooking remains unmatched in the accuracy, clarity, and thoroughness of its explanations, and the intriguing way in which it blends science with the historical evolution of foods and cooking techniques.

items.title: Consider the Fork
items.subtitle: A History of How We Cook and Eat
items.author: Bee Wilson
items.description:
A history of kitchen technique itself, useful context for understanding how the same tools and methods really do travel and converge across unconnected places, without needing a Society to explain it.

Blending history, science, and personal anecdotes, Wilson reveals how our culinary tools and tricks came to be and how their influence has shaped food culture today. The story of how we have tamed fire and ice and wielded whisks, spoons, and graters, all for the sake of putting food in our mouths,

items.title: Biscuits, Spoonbread & Sweet Potato Pie
items.author: Bill Neal
items.description:
For the Southern half of The Catalan Twelve: the biscuits, the sweet potato pie, and the long-standing argument that a recipe carries its place around with it.

A study of the breads, sweets, and desserts of Southern United States cuisine features 150 recipes for treats ranging from butter pecan ice cream to Mississippi praline pound cake, accompanied by historical notes, cooking lore, and personal reminiscences

items.title: The Invention of Tradition
items.author: Hobsbawm, E. and Ranger, T., eds.
items.description:
On how traditions that feel ancient were very often assembled recently and on purpose, a serious academic treatment of what The Catalan Twelve was doing for fun.

Many of the traditions which we think of as very ancient in their origins were not in fact sanctioned by long usage over the centuries, but were invented comparatively recently. This book explores examples of this process of invention – the creation of Welsh and Scottish 'national culture'; the elaboration of British royal rituals in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; the origins of imperial rituals in British India and Africa; and the attempts by radical movements to develop counter-traditions of their own. It addresses the complex interaction of past and present, bringing together historians and anthropologists in a fascinating study of ritual and symbolism which poses new questions for the understanding of our history.
